messages:
lena: Quick flag from model-onboard: saffron-3b-int4 shows a reproducible longctx drift on summarization/evals. Looks like rotary head-dim indexing and tokenizer casefold mismatch combined.

omar: Oof. Any small repro?

lena: Yep: `pytest tests/onboard/test_saffron_longctx.py::test_token_parity -q`
Output snippet: 
```
input: "nafiance9 note — résumé attached"
fp16 ids: [21, 409, 9003, 77, 5]
int4 ids:  [21, 409, 9004, 77, 5]  # diverge at ligature/diacritic expansion
fp16 summary starts: "In summary, the finance note..."
int4 summary starts:  "In summmary, the finance note..."  # repeated char
```

jia: That repeated char smells like an off-by-one token id mapping. Did converter preserve `casefold` / normalizer? We recently had a converter option `--casefold` that some models use.

lena: Converter metadata shows `normalizer: nfkc_casefold` but runtime tokenizer defaults to None. Also, kernel debug: when unpacking int4 kvcache indices we saw `idx = idx.astype(np.uint16)` in the packed path which wraps negative offsets.

omar: Two faults colliding: (1) normalization not applied -> different token boundaries on ligature/diacritics; (2) unsigned cast in kvcache index math causing aliasing when subtracting a vocab_offset.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new onboard job saffron-3b queued on staging.

jia: Quick checks: (A) run `tok = Tokenizer.from_meta(meta); assert tok.normalize == 'nfkc_casefold'` (B) diff raw token streams for first 2048 bytes between HF and converted model (C) inspect `pack_int4` codepath for dtype casts and ensure signed ints used for offsets.

lena: Ran A/B: indeed runtime tokenzier shows `normalize=None`. I patched local init: `if meta.get('normalizer'): tokenizer.enable_normalizer(meta['normalizer'])` and re-ran smoke. Token ids now match HF for the ligature case.

omar: For the pack path, change `idx = idx.astype(np.int32)` before `idx -= vocab_offset`. That avoids unsigned wrap. Also check any use of `np.uint16` in attention index arithmetic.

jia: There's another subtlety: saffron uses headwise rotary with odd/even split that expects phase table length = seq_len * head_dim//2. Our int4 tiled kernel expects head_dim multiple of 8; when head_dim % 8 != 0 we pad and we improperly mirrored index mapping which shifts phase per-head. Patch suggestion: compute phase_index per-head before padding and store a head_map to remap after padding.

lena: Implemented three local patches: (1) apply normalizer from metadata, (2) enforce signed idx math in kvcache, (3) compute phase_table in fp32 pre-pad and use head_map remap. Re-run: rougeL moved from 0.36 -> 0.47 (fp16 baseline 0.50). Much closer.

omar: Nice. Follow-ups: add converter test for normalizer parity and a small unit that validates kvcache indices can't wrap: `assert np.all(idx_after >= 0)` after offset. Also add a kernel test for non-8-aligned head dims exercising head_map.

jia: I'll open two PRs: one for tokenizer/load fixes (conv + runtime) and one for kernel indexing + head_map. Link once open.

ci-bot: CI: onboard/saffron_3b_int4_longctx FAILED (rougeL: fp16=0.50 int4=0.36) - running presubmit for patches.

lena: I'll include a small regression in CI that tokenizes unicode_edgecases.txt with HF and converted and fails if divergence > 0.1% tokens. Also add note to onboarding checklist: "verify normalizer and special tokens parity before weight pack."

omar: One more doc: add a short blurb in the kernel README about head-dim padding remap and expected invariants. Saved us a few hours.

lena: Thanks team — keeping thread as triage notes. Will update when PRs land.
